description: deixis scripted binding vectors — the two-stage binding of ADR 0013 §2, the outcome classes of §3 and the structural rows of §5, run on each core's native Node[T]. Binding is not a deixis API: each conformance CLI carries a scripted harness that builds and reads every tree through the core's own compose, decompose and at. A name is a byte string, spelled as hex (vectors/README.md). A node is {"own": <hex name>, "children": [[<hex key>, <node>], …]}, the spelling of vectors/MNODE-PLAN.md; paths are arrays of hex keys, and [] is ε. prepare under the context γ (a string) is §2's context-indexed map: the node at path p becomes the request {"name": <its name, the exact bytes>, "origin": γ, "at": p}, the context moved along the path to γ·p. Keys and the path set are unchanged. op prepare asserts the whole prepared tree. op at-after-prepare asserts both sides of §2's law, at(P_γ(N), p) and P_{γ·p}(at(N, p)): the CLI answers each side, and each must equal result, {"defined": …} or {"undefined": {}}. A selected subtree keeps the paths from the original root, because moving a subtree never re-roots it. binder is a script, [[<hex name>, <outcome>], …]. An outcome is {"bound": <id>}, {"refused": <reason>}, {"fault": <cause>} or {"cancelled": {}}, and a name the script does not list is {"refused": "unrecognized"}. op resolve-at prepares under context, selects path and answers {"absent": {}} when the path is missing, without consulting the binder; otherwise it answers the binder's outcome for the selected request's name. op resolve-all-or-fail is §2's eager batch: it resolves every request depth-first, a node before its children and children in ascending unsigned-octet key order, stops at the first outcome that is not bound and answers {"failed": <that outcome>}, or else {"bound-tree": <the tree of bound ids>}. Both resolving ops answer {"outcome": …, "consulted": [<hex name>, …]}, where consulted lists the names the binder was asked for, in order: §5's instrumented binder, so structural noninterference is observed rather than inferred. Hand-authored from docs/design/0013-binding-views-and-the-service-line.md as merged in c0eb86d, with docs/PATH.md for selection and vectors/MNODE-PLAN.md for spelling, and from nothing else. No implementation of these operations existed when they were written. pins are fragments of ADR 0013 that each judgment rests on, checked by tools/pincheck.py. Each note names the defect it catches. 19 cases.

cases.name: bind-prepare-whole-tree
pins: preparation preserves it exactly
cases.note: §2, P_γ(Node(n,m)) = Node(request(γ,n), {k ↦ P_{γ·[k]}(m[k])}); §5 path set. Every node, the root and the interior node [61] included, becomes a request whose at is its own path. Catches a request with no cursor or a cursor relative to its parent ([6a] instead of [61, 6a]), the empty key's cursor read as the root's ([] instead of [""]), the one key 612f62 spelled as the two keys [61, 62], and a dropped or added child.

cases.name: bind-prepare-captures-the-supplied-context
pins: Preparation is pure.
cases.note: §2: a request captures its binding scope, here the context site-b, and nothing else. A single childless node is prepared too. Catches an origin that is hard-coded or taken from the tree instead of the context, and preparation that starts below the root.

cases.name: bind-prepare-keeps-the-exact-name-bytes
pins: keeps the original name bytes
requests keep the exact bytes
cases.note: §2 and §5 original names. The root's name is the empty byte string, and it is still a name at an existing node. ff00 is not UTF-8, 414243 is ABC in capitals, 2f612f62 is /a/b and 61626300 ends in a NUL. Catches a normalized or rewritten name (case folding, UTF-8 replacement, a trimmed NUL), an empty name read as no request, and a name that spells a path moving its request: the request at [03] stays at [03], never [61, 62].

cases.name: bind-law-selection-keeps-the-captured-path
pins: Moving a subtree never re-roots it.
selecting before or after preparation gives equivalent scoped requests
cases.note: §2's law at an interior path. Both orders give requests at [61] and [61, 6a], the paths from the original root. Catches re-rooting at the selected subtree on either side of the law: requests at [] and [6a], or a select-then-prepare side that restarts the context at γ instead of moving it to γ·[61].

cases.name: bind-law-empty-key-is-a-real-child
pins: Moving a subtree never re-roots it.
cases.note: §2's law at the path of one empty key, which is not ε (PATH). Catches [""] read as ε, which selects the whole tree, and a request at the empty key whose cursor collapses to [].

cases.name: bind-law-slash-key-is-one-key
pins: Moving a subtree never re-roots it.
cases.note: §2's law at a key holding a slash byte (a/b). It is one key, so the path has length one. Catches a cursor kept as a slash-joined string and split again, which misses the node or records at as [61, 62].

cases.name: bind-law-missing-path-is-undefined-on-both-sides
pins: Both sides are undefined exactly when the source path is missing.
cases.note: §2: equal structural definedness. [62] is missing before preparation and after it. Catches a missing path answered with a placeholder request (an empty name, a default child) on either side of the law.

cases.name: bind-law-two-keys-are-not-the-slash-key
pins: Both sides are undefined exactly when the source path is missing.
cases.note: §2: the node at [61] has the one child 6a, so [61, 62] is missing, although the root holds the single key 612f62. The pair to bind-law-slash-key-is-one-key. Catches a path joined with slash bytes and looked up as one key, which would find the slash node.

cases.name: bind-resolve-missing-path-is-absent
pins: select, report structural absence if the path is missing, otherwise
cases.note: §3: a path missing from a complete tree is structural absence, reported by at, and the binder is never asked. One of three outcomes on one tree and one binder, with bind-resolve-unlisted-name-is-refused and bind-resolve-fault-is-neither-absence-nor-refusal. Catches absence reported as a refusal or a fault, and a binder consulted for a path that does not exist.

cases.name: bind-resolve-unlisted-name-is-refused
pins: An unrecognized name still occupies an existing node.
cases.note: §2, §3: the binder does not list the name at [""], so resolving it is a refusal, a defined result of an existing request. bind-law-empty-key-is-a-real-child shows prepare and at succeeding at the same node. Catches an unrecognized name turned into structural absence, and an invented capability for it.

cases.name: bind-resolve-fault-is-neither-absence-nor-refusal
pins: Failure to establish validity is not proof of invalidity.
cases.note: §3: an unreachable authority yields a fault, never an invented refusal, and the node stays an existing node. Catches a fault reported as a refusal or as a missing child (§5 failure distinctions).

cases.name: bind-resolve-through-a-refused-node
pins: selection and reconstruction resolve and invoke nothing
cases.note: §2, §5: the name at [61] is refused as expired, and the node still occupies its path, so selection walks through it to [61, 6a] and only the selected request is resolved. Catches selection that resolves each request on the way (consulted would hold the cancelled root and the expired [61]), and a refused node whose subtree reads as absent.

cases.name: bind-resolve-cancelled-at-the-root
pins: Refusal, fault and cancellation
cases.note: §2: ε selects the root, and its outcome is Cancelled, the fourth summand of BindResult, distinct from a refusal, a fault and absence. Catches cancellation folded into another outcome, and ε treated as a miss.

cases.name: bind-noninterference-missing-path-under-a-faulting-binder
pins: selection and reconstruction resolve and invoke nothing
cases.note: §5 structural noninterference. The binder faults on every name in the tree, and [61, 62] is missing below an existing node, so selection reports absence and asks the binder nothing. Catches a binder consulted before or during selection: resolving the ancestors on the way, resolving the whole tree first, or resolving the deepest existing node, each of which answers a fault or lists a name.

cases.name: bind-noninterference-the-faulting-binder-does-fault
pins: Failure to establish validity is not proof of invalidity.
cases.note: §3, §5. The pair to bind-noninterference-missing-path-under-a-faulting-binder: the same binder at an existing path does fault, so the absence there is selection's answer and not a binder that happened to stay quiet. Catches a harness whose binder never answers, which would let the noninterference case pass for the wrong reason.

cases.name: bind-eager-expired-sibling-fails-the-batch
pins: Take a tree with a live child `a` and an expired sibling `b`: the batch fails,
cases.note: §2's counterexample, first half: the live child at [61] binds and its sibling at [62] is refused as expired, so the eager batch fails. Catches a batch that skips the refused node and returns a pruned tree (§5: a refused name removes a node), and one that reports success with the failure hidden inside.

cases.name: bind-eager-counterexample-selecting-the-live-child-binds
pins: Take a tree with a live child `a` and an expired sibling `b`: the batch fails,
cases.note: §2's counterexample, second half: on the tree and binder of bind-eager-expired-sibling-fails-the-batch, selecting the live child and resolving only it binds. So whole-tree binding cannot carry the selection law. Catches resolve-at implemented as the eager batch followed by selection.

cases.name: bind-eager-all-bound-keeps-the-shape
pins: Whole-tree binding is an optional batch, never the foundation.
cases.note: §2 resolveAllOrFail: Node[BindingRequest[A]] → M(Node[A]). Every name binds, so the result is the tree of bound ids at the same paths, the empty key included. consulted is depth-first in unsigned-octet key order: the root, then "", then [61] and its child [61, 00] before ff. Catches a lost or added path, a result tree that carries names or requests instead of ids, and breadth-first, insertion or signed-octet order (each moves ff or 64656570).

cases.name: bind-eager-stops-at-the-first-failure-in-depth-first-order
pins: Whole-tree binding is an optional batch, never the foundation.
cases.note: §2, §3. The binder does not list deep (64656570, at [61, 00]), so it is refused as unrecognized, and hi at [ff] faults. Depth-first order reaches deep first, the batch stops there and hi is never asked. Catches breadth-first or reverse order and reporting the last failure (each answers hi's fault), and a batch that keeps resolving after the first failure.
